lenses.reason: The frozen source and harness are internally consistent, the 329-test receipt reports 329 passes and no failures, and the ownership/lifecycle tests cover meaningful cleanup and fault paths. The source is organized into game, render, input, UI, and audio modules. This is strong engineering evidence, but it is not a full independent client-security or dependency-supply-chain audit.
limits: I verified pinned hashes and inspected source and receipts, but did not execute the suite.
No independent security review or dependency vulnerability audit is established by the cited evidence.

findings.description: The 329 passing regressions establish broad behavioral coverage, not a security or dependency-risk assessment.
findings.acceptance: Record a focused client-security and dependency audit against this frozen candidate, including findings and disposition; rerun applicable checks if source or dependencies change.
findings.owner: code cleanup owner or primary integration

lenses.reason: Lifecycle and recovery work has substantial support: context-loss/manual-resume, model loading, disposal, and actual-browser audio recovery were checked, and both local packages were exercised on the GTX 1650 Ti through desktop and nested portable views. These checks establish successful rendering and packaging on that setup, not sustained frame rate. The known stall investigation does not prove the observed long stall is eliminated.
limits: Engine callback and draw counts are not FPS or latency measurements.
Evidence is from one reported GPU/browser environment and emulated viewports, not sustained physical-device use.
The prior multi-second stall is localized but not conclusively resolved.

findings.description: The available probe does not establish that the observed long render-submission stall is gone or that performance remains stable over an extended session.
findings.acceptance: Collect a source-pinned, sustained hardware run with frame-time distribution, worst-case stalls, and resource/lifecycle behavior; report the exact device, browser, settings, and duration. Do not use render callback totals as a substitute.
findings.owner: code cleanup owner or primary integration

findings.description: Physical-phone lifecycle, thermals, and resource behavior are not covered by the emulated touch and desktop GPU evidence.
findings.acceptance: Capture a documented physical-device session covering startup, play, interruption/recovery, and a sustained run, or state the device-specific limitation explicitly in launch materials.

lenses.reason: The source and regression suite encode deterministic sectors, opening pacing, fuel lanes, enemy/cover behavior, boss echoes, and replay-related systems. However, the round cutoff has zero credited bot episodes and zero credited realtime player episodes. Pilots do not count, and no 10-second active-view observation path was demonstrated. Therefore gameplay feel, fairness across the matrix, boss pressure, and replay pacing remain materially unsubstantiated rather than proven defective.
limits: The required final bot0/1000 and Terra Medium player0/60 are the cutoff counts.
Automated or staged captures cannot establish human feel or viewed live-play fairness.
No conclusions are drawn from the excluded running batch or its captures.

findings.description: There is no credited final campaign evidence for gameplay success, fairness, boss encounters, or replay progression.
findings.acceptance: Complete and audit the specified 1000 hardware bot episodes across the required matrix and 60 qualifying Terra Medium realtime player episodes, with source/harness identity, raw receipts, coverage, failures, and viewed observations retained.

findings.description: The active-view workflow still lacks a demonstrated cadence that supports the required observation interval; a preflight title view or staged screenshot is not an in-run observation.
findings.acceptance: Demonstrate a real active episode with the required timely view-and-note cadence, preserve image hashes and timestamps, and have the audit reject stale or unviewed captures.

lenses.reason: The reviewed static gameplay image has a coherent industrial sci-fi palette, clear environmental framing, and a legible boss silhouette and projectile lane. The packet also records accepted art and Fable's bounded ambient-traffic work with geometry, HUD-clearance, and seeded-layout contracts. These are persuasive art and rendering inputs, but static images and paired stills do not establish motion readability or visual clarity during human play.
limits: Traffic review is based on still-frame comparisons, not a continuous human-play session.
The screenshot is illustrative visual evidence, not credited gameplay.
No accepted-art contest is reopened by this review.

findings.description: Combat readability in motion, especially player/projectile contrast against the dark environment and during boss encounters, has not been demonstrated with human play evidence.
findings.acceptance: Obtain a viewed, source-pinned gameplay session spanning ordinary combat and a boss encounter; record concrete visibility issues and address only demonstrated problems without reopening accepted art.

lenses.reason: Keyboard focus/navigation, touch-state logic, reduced-motion behavior, settings persistence, short-screen presentation, and desktop/portrait/landscape layouts have meaningful source tests and staged hardware checks. But controller and touch hardware were not physically exercised, assistive-technology use is untested, and the active-view cadence gap also limits onboarding/input validation during real play.
limits: Automated input fixtures and emulated touch do not establish physical controller or phone behavior.
No assistive-technology session is evidenced.
The cited screenshot is a staged static view, not an onboarding usability test.

findings.description: Accessibility and real-device input coverage are incomplete: assistive technology, physical controller, and physical touch behavior are not demonstrated.
findings.acceptance: Record a focused keyboard/screen-reader and physical controller/touch-device walkthrough, including focus order, announcements, control discoverability, and any blocking issues; document unsupported combinations.

lenses.reason: Audio code includes lifecycle recovery and synthesized music/effects, and the packet cites actual-browser rendering and signal measurements with zero clipping/nonfinite samples plus a recovery check. Those facts support technical generation and recovery, not whether the music, mix, cue hierarchy, or effects sound good. The packet explicitly says nothing was heard.
limits: No one listened to the measured output; spectral and amplitude measurements cannot substitute for perception.
Physical mobile interruptions and recovery remain unverified.

findings.description: Musical quality, cue intelligibility, mix balance, and recovery audibility have no listening evidence at this cutoff.
findings.acceptance: Conduct and document an actual audition of the frozen build covering menu, ordinary combat, warnings/resource cues, boss, pause/recovery, and mute/settings behavior; note device/output and concrete defects.

lenses.reason: The marketing bundle is locally validated with editable assets and multiple exports, while the frozen candidate's Pages and portable Itch packages pass local file-hash and nested-path checks. This supports packaging readiness, not public distribution readiness: the packet says there was no new Pages deployment, Itch upload, or account-image update, and the public listing still points to the previous Pages release.
limits: No live account listing, uploaded build, or account-image state was verified.
Local package success does not establish public availability or preservation of the prior Itch upload.

findings.description: The candidate has not been published or verified at the public distribution endpoints; account-only actions and the current listing remain outside the local package receipts.
findings.acceptance: After all evidence gates pass, publish the approved build, verify the live Pages and Itch listing/build from a public user path, verify capsule/account imagery, and confirm the previous Itch upload is preserved.

lenses.reason: The frozen candidate has substantial lifecycle, collision, settings and release-integrity coverage; the retained regression log reports 329 passes. All 12 round-manifest files and all 96 runtime, 116 harness and 55 editable-source file hashes matched the working tree. The candidate's stated commit, source hash and harness hash match the round manifest. The production input and lifetime abstractions and fault-oriented tests show deliberate maintenance work. This is not a comprehensive security audit or proof that the tests exercise every real browser failure.
limits: Readonly review of selected source and retained receipts; tests were not rerun.
Per-file hash comparisons verify the listed files, not an independent exhaustive security audit or recomputation of aggregate fingerprint algorithms.

findings.description: Missing evidence: release security and maintainability assurance is narrower than the broad lens; passing regressions are not a dependency or threat-model audit.
findings.acceptance: Code cleanup owner or primary integration records a scoped review of production dependencies, browser-exposed surfaces, storage and build inputs; resolve material findings or document risk with ownership.

lenses.reason: The actual production and nested portable receipts show successful hardware-backed rendering and package verification, and fault-injection tests cover significant cleanup paths. Historical investigation records large submission stalls; the corrected ownership probes improve the evidence but do not establish that all stalls are eliminated. Callback and draw totals are not sustained FPS measurements.
limits: The cited stall observations include earlier checkpoints and do not independently prove the same defect remains in RC01.
Hardware checks are headless and do not establish sustained performance or physical-device behavior.

findings.description: Missing evidence: no sustained, representative RC01 frame-time and resource-lifecycle validation demonstrates that observed historical stalls are acceptably controlled.
findings.acceptance: Primary integration records candidate-bound frame-time distributions, worst stalls, GPU/device/configuration and resource trends over representative sustained play, including pause, resume and repeated runs; investigate and fix reproducible unacceptable stalls.

lenses.reason: The production code and tests cover combat and collision, and a historical pilot supplies limited loop-zero context, but the required final campaign has zero audited bot episodes and zero credited player episodes at the cutoff. No qualifying active-view path at the required cadence was demonstrated. Fairness, pacing, boss quality and replay across the prescribed bands therefore remain largely unsubstantiated rather than proven defective.
lenses.confidence: high on the evidence gap; low on subjective gameplay quality
limits: No gameplay was personally played or observed continuously in this review.
Historical pilots and staged or automated captures are not final player credit.
The running rc01-final-0000 batch and later evidence are excluded.

findings.description: Missing required evidence: audited final bot 0/1000 and credited Terra Medium player 0/60; the documented pilot did not achieve the required active-view cadence.
findings.acceptance: Primary integration establishes and demonstrates an actually viewed, timely active-play observation path, then obtains and audits the candidate-bound 1000 bot and 60 player episodes across the specified bands, including boss, pacing, failure and replay observations. Triage reproducible issues without counting pilots as final credit.

lenses.reason: The inspected production desktop and environment stills show a coherent industrial isometric world, deliberate blue-and-amber lighting, depth and recognizable route markings. This is an attractive static direction, not proof of legibility during combat or movement. In the inspected dark scenes, some small dark objects and background structures blend together; whether that harms actual target recognition is a subjective risk, not a verified gameplay defect.
lenses.confidence: medium for inspected stills; low for motion readability
limits: Stills and traffic comparison captures do not establish animation quality, combat visibility or sustained ambience.
Existing accepted art is not reopened merely because of this observation.

findings.description: Subjective risk and missing evidence: dark, small world objects may be difficult to distinguish in motion against the fortress.
findings.acceptance: Fable reviews candidate-bound continuous combat footage and player observations across relevant sectors, cameras and quality settings; only if recognition problems are demonstrated, adjust underlying lighting or asset contrast and recheck.

lenses.reason: The production source supports keyboard, gamepad and touch abstractions, and retained tests cover settings, UI ownership and short layouts. The portrait capture shows a complete touch-control layout, but the small, widely spaced HUD labels are a readability concern in this static image, not a verified physical-phone failure. Physical controller, touch and assistive-technology operation have not been established.
lenses.confidence: medium for static layout and implemented input paths; low for accessibility and physical ergonomics
limits: Emulated touch is not physical-phone testing; staged results are not normal-play replay.
No screen-reader, physical controller or hands-on touch session was reviewed.

findings.description: Missing evidence and subjective risk: physical-device input, assistive operation and small-screen readability are unverified.
findings.acceptance: Opus coordinates real phone and controller sessions and an assistive-technology/keyboard walkthrough of onboarding, settings, play and results; record device, failures and readability feedback, then fix demonstrated presentation or navigation problems.

lenses.reason: Actual-browser lifecycle and rendered-mix measurements, plus fault-injection disposal tests, provide useful technical evidence. They cannot establish whether music, effects and warnings are audible, intelligible, balanced, emotionally appropriate or recover correctly on real devices: nothing was heard in the reported sessions.
lenses.confidence: high on missing listening proof; low on perceived quality
limits: No audio was auditioned in this review or the cited measured sessions.
Headless visibility interruption and physical speaker, call interruption and controller-only unlock remain unproven.

findings.description: Missing evidence: measured audio is not an audible quality, cue-recognition or real-device recovery verdict.
findings.acceptance: Spark obtains candidate-bound human listening on representative headphones and speakers, including music/SFX balance, warning distinctness, startup gesture, mute/settings and interruption/resume; document devices and outcomes and correct confirmed issues.

lenses.reason: The local Pages and portable builds have candidate-bound package and hardware receipts, including nested iframe checks; the marketing bundle reports validated exports and editable assets. These are meaningful distribution preparations, but no account upload or live release of this candidate is evidenced, and the gameplay, audio and device gaps prevent a readiness claim. Visual brand effectiveness is not established by asset counts alone.
lenses.confidence: high on local-package versus upload distinction; medium on presentation quality
limits: A local nested iframe is not an Itch account upload or public deployment.
Marketing export validation is not an independent audience or conversion test.
This review does not authorize publication.

findings.description: Missing evidence: the candidate's account upload and actual published distribution behavior are unverified, and prerequisite release gates remain open.
findings.acceptance: Primary integration retains the verified package identity, closes the applicable release gates, and when publication is authorized records an account upload and live nested-path smoke check with matching artifact identity; Opus reviews the final store presentation.

lenses.reason: Strong, reproducible identity and test discipline: all 267 frozen file hashes match, the candidate is an ancestor of HEAD with no runtime changes since, and 329/329 regressions pass. window.KZ is correctly gated behind import.meta.env.DEV. innerHTML sinks in Screens.js/HUD.js were reviewed; the one user-influenced value (callsign) is sanitized to A-Z0-9 and no injection path was demonstrated. Deductions: the bot QA path runs against a Vite dev server and nothing rejects that for credit, so the bot evidence is not provenance-bound to the production bundle; large files (Audio.js 1658 lines, Game.js 1578) and ad hoc innerHTML templates without a shared escape helper raise maintenance cost.
limits: Did not run tests; relied on the recorded 329-pass log with matching hashes.
Security review is limited to static grep and sink inspection; no dynamic testing.
Did not read rc01-final-0000 (excluded from this round).

findings.description: Bot campaign provenance: run-bot.cjs spawns node_modules/vite/bin/vite.js (dev server) and waits for window.KZ, which main.js sets only when import.meta.env.DEV. credit.cjs checks only kind==='final-candidate' and campaign-report.cjs has no build-mode or served-bundle check. Pre-cutoff bot config.json files all record a local 127.0.0.1 Vite URL. Credited bot episodes therefore would not be from the frozen production bundle that Pages and Itch ship.
findings.acceptance: Final bot and live records must come from a served production build whose served file hashes match the frozen candidate (e.g. vite build plus a hash-verified static server, with a QA hook that does not depend on DEV). credit.cjs and campaign-report.cjs must reject any record whose served build is not that production bundle. Demonstrate on a non-credited pilot that the audit rejects a dev-server record and accepts a production-served one.
findings.owner: primary (scripts/qa/launch); code cleanup owner for any production-safe QA hook in src/main.js

findings.description: Maintainability: Audio.js (1658 lines) and Game.js (1578 lines) are very large single-owner modules; dynamic HTML is built with template strings through innerHTML in Screens.js (lines ~443, 514, 519) and HUD.js (~188-193) with no shared escape helper. Safe today by construction, not by a common guard.
findings.acceptance: Split or document module boundaries for the two large files without changing behavior (regressions must stay 329/329 and hashes must be re-frozen). Route dynamic values in innerHTML through one escape helper or textContent, with a test that a crafted callsign or label cannot inject markup.
findings.owner: code cleanup owner (Sol XHigh thread); primary if no owner is active

lenses.reason: Lifecycle handling is careful and verifiable in source: blur and visibility suspend input (Input.js), Engine.js handles webglcontextlost/restored with a manual resume, dispose() chains cover engine, input, postfx, renderer, and game owners, and audio resumes on gesture with a retry. Hardware pass is recorded on a GTX 1650 Ti via NitroBliss Chrome 157 in production and nested-iframe runs with zero page/network errors. Deductions: render-submission stalls remain unexplained (pilot max submission 431.6 ms and 290.1 ms, a 3.1 s observation stall with no confirmed cause), no sustained FPS was measured, and physical phone behavior is untested.
limits: Render counts are not FPS; no sustained frame-rate measurement exists for this candidate.
Headless hardware browser only; no physical phone or tablet.
Stall causes are reported as unisolated in the cited docs; I did not reproduce them.

findings.description: Observed-viewing cadence is unsolved on the evidence. PARALLEL-PILOT-01 shows the view-note age at 41.7 s; the assessment concludes the single-frame tool path acknowledges in about 13-14 s against a 10 s requirement. The required 60 live observations are at 0/60.
findings.acceptance: A non-credited pilot where audit-live.cjs shows actual-view acknowledgment spacing at or under 10 s across a full episode, using an image-returning tool path, followed by the final 60 live observations passing the same audit. No final live run until the pilot passes.
findings.owner: primary (live tooling and audit); not a Fable, Opus, or Spark item

findings.description: Unexplained render-submission stalls: pilot-stall-high-to-medium-01 max submission 431.6 ms, pilot-stall-medium-boot-01 290.1 ms, and a 3.1 s stall localized to observation o001. The cited fix reuses retained program IDs, but the docs state it does not prove stalls are eliminated.
findings.acceptance: A per-frame submit-timing trace on the frozen candidate under the same hardware path, showing p95 and max submission times within a stated budget across a full episode, with any residual stall attributed to a cause. Otherwise state the residual stall as a known limit in the judging packet.
findings.owner: code cleanup owner for the reliability investigation; Fable for any material or geometry changes it requires

lenses.reason: The design and implementation have substance: the difficulty law in src/world/Level.js matches the stated formula (threat multiplied by 1+0.3*loop, clamped at 2.2; difficultyAt multiplied by 1+0.35*loop), and the sector, boss, and fortress structure is implemented. The evidence for fairness and pacing is nearly absent: 0 credited bot episodes of 1000, 0 credited player episodes of 60, and one genuine loop-0 victory in a development pilot (not credited). Pilots show early deaths (e.g. the 511-frame sector-0 death). Subjective feel and replay have no human evidence.
limits: No credited episode of any kind exists at this cutoff, so gameplay balance cannot be judged from outcome data.
Feel is subjective and no human play was recorded.
The bot runs on the dev build (see L1-F1), so even future bot outcomes are not yet production-bound.

findings.description: No credited gameplay at the cutoff: bot 0/1000 and Terra Medium player 0/60, with no human-play record. Pilot outcomes cannot be attributed as fairness or pacing results.
findings.acceptance: Complete the final bot allocation (180 each at loops 0, 1, 2, 3, 7; 100 at loop 30) on a production-bound build with campaign-report.cjs passing, and complete 10 live observed episodes per band (60 total) under the audited observation contract. Report per-band outcome distributions and failed-seed repros.
findings.owner: primary (bot campaign and report); Terra Medium (live player runs)

findings.description: Grade bookkeeping discrepancy on record: the fast single pilot shows grade slots 1 and 7 displayed as C while trials.jsonl records grades only for sectors 0-1 and no boss or rack progression. The cause is unisolated; the observation assessment says it is not demonstrated to be a renderer misalignment.
findings.acceptance: A regression test that grade display and grade bookkeeping agree on a seeded loop-30 fixture, or a documented explanation that the display is correct and the record is stale. Confirm the closing state on the candidate before final runs.
findings.owner: code cleanup owner for Game.js grade bookkeeping; Opus only if the fault is in result presentation

lenses.reason: The staged captures I viewed show a coherent, distinctive look: a lit Iron Sentinel boss on a fortress deck with readable lane and hazard lines and a clear HUD in 01-iron-sentinel, and a gun-battery highway with a purple skyline, distinct sector identity, and legible fuel canisters in 04-gun-batteries. Ambient traffic evidence exists. The user has accepted the gunner and art set. Deductions: evidence is stills at 1920x1080 only; there is no continuous motion, small-phone readability check, or live-play frame, and the marketing frames are explicitly staged.
limits: Two of five screenshots reviewed plus proof-packet summaries; I did not review the other captures.
Staged teleport captures, not gameplay; the listing says so.
No continuous motion evidence or phone-sized readability check for the world.

findings.description: Readability at phone size and during motion has not been evaluated with a gameplay frame: the HUD in the 1920x1080 stills is legible, but its smallest labels are 8-11 px in CSS and the phone layout is not sampled in art evidence.
findings.acceptance: One 390x844 and one 844x390 live gameplay still with HUD and a 5 s continuous clip, checked for shape and label readability, with notes on any legibility fault.
findings.owner: Fable for world and lighting readability; Opus for HUD label size

lenses.reason: The UI work is careful in the code: aria roles and live regions on HUD and grades, aria-hidden and inert handling for screens and touch controls, focus-visible outlines, reduced-motion overrides across many blocks, 44 px touch targets on touch devices, device-matched control legends on title, and gamepad menu walking. Known defects remain: on short viewports the results TOTAL row and callsign field sit under the sticky action bar until scrolled or walked to, which the packet records as a limit. There is no text-size option, no colorblind palette, and no key remapping (KEYMAP is fixed in Input.js). Physical controller, touch, and assistive-technology use are untested.
limits: Touch and gamepad were emulated in Chrome; no physical phone or controller.
No assistive-technology session (screen reader or switch) was run.
Results-screen fix verified in staged runs only, not in a normal-play replay.

findings.description: Results screen on short viewports (667x375 touch, 390x844): the TOTAL row and callsign field sit under the sticky action bar until the user scrolls or walks focus to them. The packet records this as a limit, not as fixed.
findings.acceptance: Captures at 667x375 and 390x844 showing the TOTAL row and callsign field fully visible without scrolling, or a documented placement change, with the staged results regression still passing.

findings.description: Accessibility gaps: no text-size setting; no colorblind-safe palette option; no key remapping (fixed KEYMAP in Input.js line 11); several HUD labels at 8-11 px (style.css line 301 uses 8 px for grade index digits).
findings.acceptance: Either ship at least a text-size option and a legible-minimum rule (for example 12 px for HUD labels on touch), plus a documented decision on remapping and colorblind palettes, or state these as explicit known limits in the packet and listing.
findings.owner: Opus High for text size and palette (UI); code cleanup owner for key remapping in Input.js

findings.description: No physical controller, touch-device, or assistive-technology session exists; all coverage is emulated or staged.
findings.acceptance: One physical phone and one physical gamepad session with observed notes, and a screen-reader pass of the title and settings flow, recorded with their limits. Account and device constraints are outside the repository.
findings.owner: primary, with the account or device owner

lenses.reason: Audio code is substantial and carefully scoped: trusted-gesture unlock with retry, context suspend and resume on visibility, a separate missile-lock cue, and disposal tests. The candidate-bound 32 s OfflineAudioContext audition has peak -5.32 dBFS, zero clipped or non-finite samples, and no page errors. This is measurement, not perception. No person or agent has listened, and the headless tab never exercised a real hidden-tab or phone-call interruption, so recovery is untested in practice.
limits: No listening of any kind; no speaker or headphone audition.
The audition is a scripted cue program rendered offline, not a live gameplay mix capture.
Hidden-tab and phone-call recovery untested; the lifecycle runs stayed visible and Escape was not blocked.
The audition render was on source d90d5ec; the candidate c0ee294 has the same sourceHash, so runtime files are identical.

findings.description: The mix has never been heard. Peak, RMS, and clipping measurements do not establish cue audibility, balance, fatigue, or priority under dense combat.
findings.acceptance: A human listening audition of audition.wav on headphones and a laptop speaker, with notes on each labelled cue (missile lock, damage confirm, boss roar, warning priority), plus one live hardware session recording the audio state across a tab switch and resume.
findings.owner: Spark (any cue or mix changes); primary to arrange the listening and live session

findings.description: Recovery after interruption is untested in practice: the lifecycle receipts stayed visible and Escape was not blocked, so the hidden-tab policy path and the phone-call path are not exercised.
findings.acceptance: A hardware run that actually hides the tab or interrupts the audio context, showing ctx.state transitions and a successful resume on a trusted gesture, with the receipt retained.
findings.owner: primary (QA run); Spark if the recovery path needs a code change

lenses.reason: The title and listing copy are clear and consistent with the code (eight sectors, one boss, three camera rigs, device-matched legend). Marketing exports have sha256 manifests and an explicit staged-capture disclosure in ITCH-LISTING.md, which is honest. The portable ZIP hash matches its receipt and passes local nested verification. Readiness is weak: the live Itch listing still links to Pages with zero screenshots, nothing is uploaded or applied, the compositor renders typography with DejaVu rather than the in-game font, and the new portable package has not been published. The gate requires publication to be authorized, and it is not.
limits: No live listing change, upload, or deployment exists; the listing is unapplied and no account action was observed.
Did not open the live Itch page this round.
Market or community reception is not evidence in this round.

findings.description: Distribution readiness: the live Itch listing links to Pages with no screenshots and no HTML5 upload; the ITCH-LISTING.md changes are unapplied; the verified portable ZIP has not been uploaded to the account.
findings.acceptance: The account owner applies the listing, screenshots, and ZIP (keeping the previous build as rollback) and a post-upload inspection confirms the listing and the iframe render with no errors. Until then, no launch-readiness claim is made.
findings.owner: account owner (user), with primary coordinating the upload and inspection

findings.description: Export typography fallback: the cover, banner, and OG exports were composed in headless Linux with DejaVu Sans Mono, not the Cascadia or SF Mono used in game, so exported title type differs from the shipped one.
findings.acceptance: Re-export the title and cover typography with an in-game-matched font stack on the target platform, or document the substitution on the export page and in the listing.
